find_tasks.description: Find tasks by free text, ranked by relevance. This is the tool for "the task where I…", a remembered title, or any wording the user gives you — search_tasks cannot match text, it only filters. Start here whenever you do not already hold the taskId, then pass the id you found to get_task or get_timeline. Results mix two kinds of hit: task hits carry taskId and title, memo hits carry hitType="memo" with the memo body and the task it sits on, so a note the user wrote can lead you to the task. Nothing matches when the words are not in the title or in a memo; widen to search_events, which searches the full body of every event.

q.description: The words to look for in task titles and memo bodies. Use the user's own wording first; drop to one or two distinctive words if that finds nothing.

limit.description: Max hits to return, 1 to 100, default 20. Ranked best-first, so a small limit is usually enough.

search_tasks.description: List the user's tasks newest-first, filtered but never searched by text — use find_tasks when the user described a task in words. total tells you how many match the filter before you page, so check it first and narrow instead of paging blindly. Most tasks are subagent runs the user never sees: pass root="true" to get only the top-level tasks they actually work on. Narrow further with status (running/waiting/completed/errored), origin (user/server-sdk), archived, or a parentTaskId to look inside one task's subagents. Page with cursor: pass the response's nextCursor back as cursor until it is null. limit is up to 100 per page, default 30. Every page you pull stays in your context and slows the rest of the turn, so pull the narrowest set that answers the question.

status.description: Keep only tasks in this lifecycle state: running, waiting, completed, or errored. Omit to see every state.

origin.description: Keep only tasks started by "user" (the person working) or "server-sdk" (this system's own agent runs). Omit to see both.

archived.description: Pass "true" to list archived tasks instead of live ones. Omit to list only live tasks.

root.description: Pass "true" to keep only top-level tasks and drop the subagent runs the user never sees. Use it unless the question is about subagents.

parentTaskId.description: Keep only the subagent runs launched inside this task. Use it to look inside one task instead of listing everything.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextCursor. Omit to start from the newest page.

limit.description: Max tasks in this page, 1 to 100, default 30. Every row you pull stays in your context, so ask for the narrowest page that answers the question.

get_task.description: Get one task by taskId: its header (title, status, origin, workspace, parent, timestamps), its runtime sessions, and a resumeTarget when the task can be resumed. Call this after find_tasks or search_tasks to load the details of a single task the user asked about. It answers what the task is, not what happened in it — read get_timeline for that.

taskId.description: The task to load, as returned by find_tasks or search_tasks.

get_timeline.description: Get a page of a task's timeline (user messages, assistant messages, tool runs and derived activity) and read what actually happened in it. Pass taskId; page with cursor until nextCursor is null. order decides which end you start from: the default "desc" gives the newest entries first and answers "where did this end up", while "asc" starts at the very first entry and is what you want for "how did this start", "what did the user originally ask", or any retelling in order. limit is up to 500 per page, default 100. A long task is far more timeline than you need: pick the end that answers the question and take one page, or search_events with this taskId when you are after one specific moment.

taskId.description: The task whose timeline to read.

order.description: Which end to read from: "asc" starts at the task's first entry and moves forward, "desc" (the default) starts at the newest and moves back.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextCursor. Keep passing the same order with it. Omit to start from the end that order names.

limit.description: Max timeline entries in this page, 1 to 500, default 100.

get_event.description: Get one event by eventId with its full body, kind, lane, tool name, touched file paths and the task and turn it belongs to. Two uses: expand a hit from search_events or get_timeline whose body was cut short, and confirm an eventId is real and is the moment you think it is before you anchor a rule to it with propose_rule_write. An event that belongs to someone else reads as not found.

eventId.description: The event to load, as returned by search_events, get_timeline, list_memos or get_rule_evidence.

search_events.description: Full-text search across the body of every indexed event (and matching memos), ranked by relevance and recency. This is the widest reach you have: use it to find corrections, instructions, or a specific moment across many tasks, and to fall back when find_tasks matched nothing. Narrow q with taskId, lane (which kind of work), kind (which event type), toolName (which tool ran), and a from/to time range — filters cost nothing and cut what lands in your context. Page the same query with offset. limit is up to 100, default 20. Results are a mix: event hits and memo hits (marked hitType). Bodies come back trimmed, so call get_event on a hit that matters.

q.description: Free-text query matched against event titles and bodies. Omit to browse by filters alone.

taskId.description: Keep only hits inside this task. Omit to search across all of the user's tasks.

kind.description: Keep only events of this kind, for example execute_tool or agent_tracer.user.message.

lane.description: Keep only events in this lane: user, assistant, exploration, planning, implementation, questions, todos, background, coordination, telemetry, or rule.

from.description: Keep only events at or after this ISO-8601 timestamp.

to.description: Keep only events at or before this ISO-8601 timestamp.

toolName.description: Keep only events produced by this tool, for example Bash, Edit or Read. Use it when the question is about what a particular tool did rather than about words that were said.

limit.description: Max hits to return, 1 to 100, default 20.

offset.description: How many top-ranked hits to skip, default 0. Repeat the same query with offset raised by limit to read the next page. Ranking puts the best hits first, so page only when the first page truly did not answer the question.

list_memos.description: List memos the user wrote. With no arguments it returns every memo; pass taskId to scope to one task, and additionally eventId to get the memos threaded on a single event. Use this to recall notes the user attached to their work.

taskId.description: Keep only memos on this task. Omit to list every memo the user wrote.

eventId.description: Keep only the memos threaded on this single event. Pass it together with taskId when the user asks about one moment.

list_rules.description: List the verification rules that govern the user's work. Pass taskId to see the global and task-scoped rules that apply to that task, or all="true" to list every rule the user has. Each rule carries its expectation, review state, and latest verdict status. Use this to explain what rules apply or why one is unmet.

taskId.description: The task whose applicable rules to list, both global and task-scoped.

all.description: Pass "true" to list every rule the user has instead of the ones that apply to one task. Do not combine it with taskId.

get_rule_evidence.description: Get the ledger evidence behind one rule's verdict by ruleId (optionally scoped to a taskId): the anchor event, the current status, and the trigger and expectation events that decided it, each with the text and how it matched. Use this after list_rules to show why a rule is satisfied or unmet.

ruleId.description: The rule whose verdict you want the ledger evidence for, as returned by list_rules.

taskId.description: Narrow the evidence to one task when the rule is global and has verdicts on several tasks.

list_tags.description: List the user's tags with their color, description, and how many tasks each is applied to. Use this to answer questions about how the user organizes their tasks.

find_recipes.description: Find recipes (reusable workflows distilled from past tasks) by free text, ranked by relevance. Each hit is deliberately thin — recipeId, title, intent, description and score — so you can weigh several without carrying their steps. Use this whenever the user describes a kind of work rather than naming a recipe, then call get_recipe on the one you chose. It searches only recipes the user has accepted, so a candidate awaiting their decision never appears here: reach for list_recipes with a status when the question is about candidates. Nothing matching does not mean the user has no recipe on the subject.

q.description: The work to look for, in the user's own words. Describe the task, not the recipe's title.

limit.description: Max hits to return, 1 to 10, default 3. Ranked best-first, so the default is usually enough to pick one.

get_recipe.description: Get one recipe in full by recipeId: its intent, description, ordered steps, pitfalls, governing rules, touched files, status and application stats. Call this after find_recipes to explain or follow a single workflow, instead of pulling every recipe with list_recipes.

recipeId.description: The recipe to load, as returned by find_recipes or list_recipes.

list_recipes.description: List the user's recipes in full (intent, steps, pitfalls, touched files, application stats), optionally filtered by status (candidate/active/dismissed/superseded/retired). This is the only way to see recipes that are not active, so use it for "what candidates are waiting" or "how many are active" — questions about the set itself. To answer a question about a kind of work, use find_recipes and then get_recipe: this listing has no limit and every recipe it returns stays in your context in full.

status.description: Keep only recipes in this state: candidate, active, dismissed, superseded, or retired. Omit to list every recipe.

list_cleanup_suggestions.description: List task-cleanup suggestions produced for the user, optionally filtered by status (pending/accepted/dismissed). Each names the task it targets, the proposed change, and the rationale. Use this to report what cleanup the system has proposed.

status.description: Keep only suggestions in this state: pending, accepted, or dismissed. Omit to list every suggestion.

get_job.description: Get one AI job by jobId: its kind, executor, status, attempt count, the task it ran against, and its input/result/usage. Use this to report on the outcome of an agent job the user is asking about.

jobId.description: The AI job to report on.

recall_facts.description: List the durable facts you have remembered about this user, each a short key and its content. Takes no arguments and runs immediately. These same facts are already injected at the top of your context each turn; call this only to re-read them explicitly, for example before deciding whether to remember_fact a new one.

remember_fact.description: Remember a durable fact about this user that should persist across ALL of their chat threads — a stated preference or a stable detail about how they work, not a one-off detail of the current task. Pass a short slug key (for example "preferred_language") and the content; remembering the same key again overwrites it. This outlives the current thread, so it is proposed and saved only after the user approves it; say that you have proposed remembering it, not that you have remembered it.

key.description: Short slug naming the fact, for example "preferred_language". Remembering the same key again overwrites the old content.

content.description: The fact itself, written so it still makes sense in a different thread weeks from now.

enqueue_job.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, and running it starts a real, metered agent run that costs money): launch an AI job. kind is one of title.suggestion (auto-title a task), recipe.scan (distill a recipe from a task), task.cleanup (suggest cleanup across tasks). input is a JSON object with the fields that kind needs: title.suggestion takes {"taskId":"..."}; recipe.scan takes {"taskId":"..."} plus optional userPrompt, language, and trigger (dashboard/session); task.cleanup takes {} or {"filters":{"maxSuggestions":N}}. Queued until the user approves — never claim the job has started yet.

kind.description: Which job to launch: title.suggestion, recipe.scan, or task.cleanup.

input.description: JSON object carrying what that kind needs, for example {"taskId":"..."} for title.suggestion and recipe.scan.

propose_task_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): change one task. action picks what to do — update changes title and/or status, archive hides it, unarchive brings it back, delete removes it. taskId is always required; update needs at least one of title or status. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do with the task: update, archive, unarchive, or delete.

title.description: The new title. Omit to leave the title as it is.

status.description: The new lifecycle state: running, waiting, completed, or errored. Omit to leave the status as it is.

propose_memo_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): write one memo. action picks what to do — create adds a memo to a task, update rewrites one, delete removes one. create needs taskId and body, update needs memoId and body, delete needs memoId. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do with the memo: create, update, or delete.

taskId.description: The task the memo belongs to.

eventId.description: Thread the memo on this single event. Omit to attach it to the task as a whole.

propose_rule_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): write one rule. action picks what to do — create declares a rule anchored to an event, update rewrites one, delete removes one, approve promotes a proposed rule, reevaluate runs it again over its evidence. create needs taskId, anchorEventId, name and expectation; the rest need ruleId. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do with the rule: create, update, delete, approve, or reevaluate.

anchorEventId.description: The single utterance the rule hangs on, normally the user message that stated the request.

name.description: Short human-readable name for the rule.

expectation.description: JSON object saying what must happen: {"kind":"command","commandMatches":[...]}, {"kind":"pattern","pattern":"...","tool":"..."}, or {"kind":"action","tool":"..."}.

severity.description: How hard an unmet rule pushes back: info, warn, or block. Omit to take the server's default.

rationale.description: Why the rule exists, shown to the user when the verdict is unmet.

propose_tag_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): write one tag or a task's tag set. action picks what to do — create adds a tag, update renames or recolors one, delete removes one, assign replaces the whole tag set of one task. create needs name, update and delete need tagId, assign needs taskId and tagIds. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do: create, update or delete a tag, or assign replaces one task's whole tag set.

name.description: The tag name the user will see.

color.description: Lowercase #rrggbb hex color. Omit to let the server pick one.

description.description: What the tag is for. Omit when the name already says it.

taskId.description: The task whose tags to replace.

tagIds.description: JSON array of tag ids that becomes the task's full tag set. An empty array detaches every tag.

propose_recipe_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): settle one recipe candidate. action picks what to do — accept adopts it, dismiss drops it, retire withdraws one already in use. recipeId is always required. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do with the recipe candidate: accept, dismiss, or retire.

recipeId.description: The recipe to accept, activating it.

propose_cleanup_write.description: PROPOSAL (requires user confirmation, does not run immediately): settle one cleanup suggestion. action picks what to do — accept archives the suggested tasks, dismiss drops the suggestion. suggestionId is always required. The change is queued and only applied after the user approves; tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation.

action.description: What to do with the cleanup suggestion: accept or dismiss.

suggestionId.description: The cleanup suggestion to accept and apply.

failures.toolFailed: Tool {tool} failed: {reason}. Do not call it again more than once. Continue with what you already know, and tell the user plainly which information you could not read.

proposalNote: Queued for user confirmation. This action has NOT run yet and will only run after the user approves it. Tell the user you are awaiting their confirmation; never claim the change is already done.
approvalReportNote: The user approved the action above and it has now run. Tell them what it did, grounded in that result, and do not propose it again.

bindings.meaning: 도구 이름은 자기 자리 하나를 갖고, action 을 받는 도구는 그 action 마다 자리를 갖는다. 두 축이 같은 이름과 같은 action 에서 같은 자리를 불러야 한다.
